newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day t-bill rate rises to 10.822 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day t-bill rate rises to 10.822 pct.

text.p: The Philippine 91-day treasury bill rate rose to 10.822 percent at the regular weekly auction on Monday, up from 10.39 percent the previous week, the Bureau of Treasury said.
The yield on the 182-day bills rose to 11.475 percent from 10.84 while the 364-day bills went up to 11.933 percent from 11.489.
Tenders worth 5.465 billion pesos were received for the 91-day bills. The 182-day bills fetched tenders amounting to 5.205 billion and the 364-days got 7.456 billion pesos.
Tenders accepted by the Treasury were worth one billion pesos for 91-days, 1.5 billion for 182-days and two billion for 364-days.
The rise in the T-bill rates was fuelled by a 0.5 percentage-point increase in the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate to 11.5 percent on Monday, National Treasurer Caridad Valdehuesa said.
It was the second increase in less than a week. Last Wednesday, the Central Bank raised the overnight borrowing rate by 0.75 percentage points.
The move was intended to quell peso speculation as banks became wary over capital flight from stock market divestments.
But the rise in the T-bill rate was tempered by the low inflation rate of 4.6 percent in April and the very liquid financial system, Valdehuesa said.
Banks were expecting an increase of 0.60 percentage points for the 91-day T-bill rate compared with the actual increase of 0.432 percentage points, she said.
Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza told Reuters: "This (the raising of the Central Bank's key overnight rate) is a temporary action. We will continue to monitor the market daily."
He said he was heartened by the rally in the stock market and hoped it was on its way to recovery.

"I would say the action the Central Bank has done was enough to quell speculation. If the market continues to persist, I believe the market has been given enough hints to what the Central Bank can do," he said.
"We have the weapon, the arsenal to quell peso speculation," Edeza added.
